title: The language of smartphone addiction
titleChinese: 从“手机瘾”衍生出的新词
paragraphs: Are you addicted to your smartphone? Do you check your phablet in the middle of the night? Do you post to social media as you stroll along the pavement?

If you do the latter, you would be called a ‘smombie‘ in Germany. It’s a portmanteau word which combines ’smartphone‘ and ’zombie‘, and refers to the familiar sight of someone pottering along, eyes glued to the phone in their hand, oblivious to the world around them.

The term was chosen as Youth Word of the Year in Germany in 2015. Indeed, just as mobile phones have changed the way we communicate, they’ve also enriched the stock of slang that describes human behaviour.

Another such term is ‘phubbing‘. Again, it’s a combination of two individual words, this time ’phone‘ and ’snubbing‘. Picture the scene: you’re out at a cafe with a friend, but instead of listening to your scintillating conversation, he‘s engrossed in his mobile phone. We’ve all been there.
Then there‘s a phrase which comes from Chinese: the ’bowed head tribe‘. This describes not a mere, singular smombie, but the legions of people we see stooped over mobile phones.
And over in Japan, one blogger describes the groups of people dangerously traversing busy intersections as ’dumbwalkers‘, but who somehow manage to avoid crashing into each other.

While many of these terms are light-hearted, there’s a serious side. In the German city of Augsburg one phone user was killed after being hit by a tram as she crossed the road. It prompted authorities to install ground-level traffic lights for those looking down at their phones.
And the risks with phones don‘t end there. The desire for increasingly daring selfies has led to the deaths of over 120 people since 2014. That’s more than have died from shark attacks.

It may come as no surprise to hear, therefore, that we‘re more addicted to our phones than ever before, according to a survey in the UK by Deloitte. Phones are our cameras, our calendars and our windows into the constantly updating lives of friends across social media.
Without our phones by our side, surely we’d miss out on all this fun? And yes, you guessed it, there‘s a slang term for that mentality too: ’fomo‘, or the ’fear of missing out‘.

vocabulary.entry: addicted to [phr.] /əˈdɪktɪd tuː/ 沉迷于；对……上瘾
vocabulary.example: Many teenagers are addicted to their smartphones.
vocabulary.translation: 许多青少年沉迷于智能手机。

vocabulary.entry: phablet [n.] /ˈfæblət/ 平板手机 (新词；口语)
vocabulary.example: She uses a phablet for both calls and browsing.
vocabulary.translation: 她用平板手机打电话和浏览网页。

vocabulary.entry: smombie [n.] /ˈsmɒmbi/ 低头族僵尸 (新词；口语)
vocabulary.example: The street is full of smombies staring at their screens.
vocabulary.translation: 街上到处都是盯着屏幕的低头族僵尸。

vocabulary.entry: portmanteau [n.] /pɔːtˈmæntəʊ/ 合成词 (语言学词汇)
vocabulary.example: “Brunch” is a portmanteau of “breakfast” and “lunch”.
vocabulary.translation: “Brunch”是“breakfast”和“lunch”的合成词。

vocabulary.entry: pottering [v.] /ˈpɒtərɪŋ/ 闲逛；磨蹭 (英式英语；口语；原形: potter)
vocabulary.example: He spent the afternoon pottering in the garden.
vocabulary.translation: 他一下午都在花园里闲逛。

vocabulary.entry: glued to [phr.] /ɡluːd tuː/ 紧盯着；全神贯注于
vocabulary.example: The children were glued to the television.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们紧盯着电视。

vocabulary.entry: oblivious to [phr.] /əˈblɪviəs tuː/ 对……浑然不觉 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
vocabulary.translation: 他对周围的噪音浑然不觉。

vocabulary.entry: phubbing [n.] /ˈfʌbɪŋ/ 低头症 (新词；口语)
vocabulary.example: Phubbing is considered rude in social situations.
vocabulary.translation: 在社交场合低头看手机被认为是不礼貌的。

vocabulary.entry: snubbing [n.] /ˈsnʌbɪŋ/ 冷落；怠慢
vocabulary.example: His snubbing of his old friends was hurtful.
vocabulary.translation: 他对老朋友的冷落很伤人。

vocabulary.entry: scintillating [adj.] /ˈsɪntɪleɪtɪŋ/ 妙趣横生的；才华横溢的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She gave a scintillating performance on stage.
vocabulary.translation: 她在舞台上奉献了一场妙趣横生的表演。

vocabulary.entry: engrossed in [phr.] /ɪnˈɡrəʊst ɪn/ 全神贯注于
vocabulary.example: She was engrossed in her novel.
vocabulary.translation: 她全神贯注于她的小说。

vocabulary.entry: bowed head tribe [n.] /ˌbaʊd ˈhed traɪb/ 低头族 (口语；新词)
vocabulary.example: The bowed head tribe is a common sight on public transport.
vocabulary.translation: 公共交通上低头族很常见。

vocabulary.entry: legions [n. pl.] /ˈliːdʒənz/ 大批；众多 (书面语；单数: legion)
vocabulary.example: Legions of fans attended the concert.
vocabulary.translation: 大批粉丝参加了音乐会。

vocabulary.entry: stooped over [phr.] /stuːpt ˈəʊvə/ 俯身；弯腰
vocabulary.example: He was stooped over his desk, working.
vocabulary.translation: 他俯身在办公桌前工作。

vocabulary.entry: dumbwalkers [n. pl.] /ˈdʌmwɔːkəz/ 愚蠢的步行者 (新词；口语；单数: dumbwalker)
vocabulary.example: Dumbwalkers often cause accidents in busy streets.
vocabulary.translation: 愚蠢的步行者在繁忙的街道上经常引发事故。

vocabulary.entry: traversing [v.] /trəˈvɜːsɪŋ/ 穿过；横越 (书面语；原形: traverse)
vocabulary.example: They traversed the mountain range on foot.
vocabulary.translation: 他们步行穿越了山脉。

vocabulary.entry: prompted [v.] /prɒmptɪd/ 促使；引起 (原形: prompt)
vocabulary.example: The incident prompted an investigation.
vocabulary.translation: 这一事件引发了一次调查。

vocabulary.entry: selfies [n. pl.] /ˈselfiz/ 自拍照 (口语；单数: selfie)
vocabulary.example: She takes selfies wherever she goes.
vocabulary.translation: 她走到哪里都自拍。

vocabulary.entry: mentality [n.] /menˈtæləti/ 心态；心理 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He has a positive mentality towards challenges.
vocabulary.translation: 他对挑战持积极心态。

vocabulary.entry: fomo [n.] /ˈfəʊməʊ/ 错失恐惧症 (新词；口语；缩写)
vocabulary.example: Social media can trigger fomo in many people.
vocabulary.translation: 社交媒体会引发许多人的错失恐惧症。

vocabulary.entry: fear of missing out [phr.] /fɪər əv ˈmɪsɪŋ aʊt/ 害怕错过
vocabulary.example: His constant phone checking is due to fear of missing out.
vocabulary.translation: 他不停查看手机是因为害怕错过。

vocabulary.entry: slang [n.] /slæŋ/ 俚语
vocabulary.example: “Cool” is a slang word for “excellent”.
vocabulary.translation: “Cool”是表示“极好”的俚语。

vocabulary.entry: ground-level [adj.] /ˌɡraʊnd ˈlevəl/ 地面的
vocabulary.example: Ground-level traffic lights help pedestrians looking at phones.
vocabulary.translation: 地面交通信号灯帮助看手机的行人。

vocabulary.entry: calendar [n.] /ˈkælɪndə/ 日历
vocabulary.example: She uses her phone as a calendar to track appointments.
vocabulary.translation: 她用手机当日历记录约会。

vocabulary.entry: constantly [adv.] /ˈkɒnstəntli/ 不断地；总是
vocabulary.example: He is constantly checking his messages.
vocabulary.translation: 他不停地查看信息。

sentences.chinese: 你会在沿着人行道漫步时往社交媒体上发消息吗？

sentences.chinese: 如果你做了后者，在德国你会被称为“低头族僵尸”。

sentences.chinese: 另一个这样的词是“低头症”。

sentences.chinese: 我们都经历过这种情况。

sentences.chinese: 然后还有一个来自中文的短语：“低头族”。

sentences.chinese: 这个词描述的不是个体的低头族僵尸，而是我们看到的众多的俯身低头看手机的人。

sentences.chinese: 虽然这些词很多都带有轻松幽默的意味，但也有严肃的一面。

sentences.chinese: 在德国城市奥格斯堡，一名手机用户在过马路时被有轨电车撞倒后身亡。

sentences.english: It prompted authorities to install ground-level traffic lights for those looking down at their phones.
sentences.chinese: 这促使当局为那些低头看手机的人安装了地面交通信号灯。

sentences.chinese: 这个数字比死于鲨鱼袭击的人数还要多。

sentences.chinese: 因此，根据德勤在英国进行的一项调查，我们比以往任何时候都更沉迷于手机，这个消息可能听起来并不令人惊讶。

sentences.chinese: 手机是我们的相机，我们的日历，也是我们通过社交媒体了解朋友们不断更新生活的窗口。

sentences.chinese: 如果我们身边没有手机，我们肯定会错过所有这些乐趣吧？
